nodes.name: Anodic Electrodeposition of Ni₃S₄/FeS@FNF
nodes.procedure: Ni₃S₄/FeS@FNF (FNF-0.5 V) heterostructures were synthesized by in situ anodic electrodeposition on FeNi Foam at 0.5 V versus Ag/AgCl under ambient conditions. The electrolyte contained S²⁻ source with HCl added to adjust pH. Anode reactions: 3 Ni + 4 S²⁻ = Ni₃S₄ + 8 e⁻ and Fe + S²⁻ = FeS + 2 e⁻. Cathode: 2 H⁺ + 2 e⁻ = H₂ (bubbles observed). Deposition time ~10 min fully covers substrate. Around 10 min of deposition, the substrate can be fully covered.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show Ni₃S₄ peaks at 2θ of 26.6°, 31.3°, 37.9°, 50.0° and 54.8° corresponding to (220), (311), (400), (511) and (440) planes (PDF#47-1739), and FeS peaks at 2θ of 17.6°, 30.1°, 39.0°, 50.4° and 53.0° corresponding to (001), (101), (111), (112) and (201) planes (PDF#15-0037).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show vibrational bands at 217, 284, 320 and 386 cm⁻¹ attributed to Ni₃S₄ and 204, 270, 384 and 470 cm⁻¹ belonging to FeS, confirming successful synthesis of Ni₃S₄/FeS heterostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Figure 1c) reveals that the vibrational bands at 217, 284, 320 and 386 cm⁻¹ low wavenumber region are attributed to the Ni₃S₄ and 204, 270, 384 and 470 cm⁻¹ belongs to FeS.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows Ni³⁺ peaks at 854.96 eV (2p₃/₂) and 872.69 eV (2p₁/₂) in Ni₃S₄/FeS with Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio of 19.08 (Ni²⁺ 4.98%); Fe doping increases Ni³⁺ content compared to pure Ni₃S₄ (Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio 12.40).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After Fe-doping, in FNF-0.5 V (Ni₃S₄/FeS), 854.96 and 872.69 eV were associated with Ni³⁺ (Figure 3b)... In Ni₃S₄/FeS, the percentage of Ni²⁺ is the smallest at 4.98%, while the value of Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ is the largest at 19.08.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ni₃S₄/FeS oxidation at 1.1-1.8 V to NiOOH with peaks at 480 and 560 cm⁻¹; partial reversibility observed after negative sweep.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4d, starting from open-circuit voltage, a series of Raman data under different potentials were tested.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 855.72 and 873.47 eV attributed to NiOOH; Fe 2p shows Fe⁰ at 706.05 eV, Fe²⁺ at 710.97/724.11 eV, Fe³⁺ at 713.62/726.22 eV; S 2p shows transformation from M-S to S-O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a, the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrums after the OER test have two centered at 855.72 and 873.47 eV are attributed to the characteristic peaks of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Fe doping inhibits NiOOH dissolution by up to seven times compared to pure Ni₃S₄.
